source_text: τῷ Λευϊτικῷ πρὸς τὸν ἱεροφάντην Μωσέα· «Λάλησον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἢν ἐγὼ δίδωμι ὑμῖν, καὶ ἀναπαύσητε τὴν γῆν, ἢν ἐγὼ δίδωμι ὑμῖν, Σάββατα τῷ Κυρίῳ· ἓξ ἔτη σπερεῖς τὸν ἀγρόν σου, καὶ ἓξ ἔτη τεμεῖς τὴν ἄμπελόν σου, καὶ συνάξεις τὸν καρπὸν αὐτῆς, τῷ δὲ ἔτει τῷ ἑβδόμῳ Σάββατα. Ἀνάπαυσις ἔσται τῇ γῇ ὑμῶν, Σάββατα τῷ Κυρίῳ. Τὸν ἀγρόν σου οὐ σπερεῖς, καὶ τὴν ἄμπελόν σου οὐ τεμεῖς, καὶ τὰ αὐτόματα ἀναβαίνοντα τοῦ ἀγροῦ σου οὐκ ἐκθερίσεις, καὶ τὴν σταφυλὴν τοῦ ἁγιάσματός σου οὐκ ἐκτρυγήσεις, ἐνιαυτὸς ἀναπαύσεως ἔσται τῇ γῇ, καὶ ἔσται τὰ Σάββατα τῆς γῆς βρώματά σοι, καὶ τῷ παιδί σου, καὶ τῇ παιδίσκῃ σου, καὶ τῷ μισθωτῷ σου, καὶ τῷ παροίκῳ τῷ προσκειμένῳ πρὸς σέ· καὶ τοῖς κτήνεσί σου, καὶ τοῖς θηρίοις τοῖς ἐν τῇ γῇ σου ἔσται πᾶν τὸ γέννημα αὐτοῦ εἰς βρῶσιν. Καὶ ἐξαριθμήσεις σεαυτῷ ἑπτὰ ἀναπαύσεις ἐτῶν, ἑπτὰ ἔτη ἑπτάκις· καὶ ἔσονταί σοι ἑπτὰ ἑβδομάδες ἐτῶν, ἐννέα καὶ τεσσαράκοντα ἔτη. Καὶ διαγγελεῖτε σάλπιγγος φωνῇ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ ὑμῶν, ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ τῇ δεκάτῃ τοῦ μηνός. Τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ ἱλασμοῦ διαγγελεῖτε σάλπιγγι ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ ὑμῶν. Καὶ ἁγιάσετε τὸ ἔτος, τὸν πεντηκοστὸν ἐνιαυτὸν, καὶ διαβοήσετε ἄφεσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς πᾶσι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν αὐτήν. Ἐνιαυτὸς ἀφέσεως σημασία αὕτη ἔσται ὑμῖν, καὶ ἀπελεύσεται εἷς ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν κτῆσιν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν πατριὰν αὐτοῦ ἀπελεύσεται.» Συνίης οὖν ὅπως ἀροῦν τε καὶ σπείρειν, καὶ ἀμπελώνων εἶναι μελεδωνοὺς ἐφίησι μὲν ὁ νόμος, πρὸ τῆς ἑβδόμης; Ἀνεῖ-σθαί γε μὴν τῆς ἐπὶ τούτοις φροντίδος προστέταχε κατὰ τὴν ἑβδόμην. Ἀνιέμεθα γὰρ σαββατίζοντες ἐν Χριστῷ καὶ τῶν ἐπιγείων ἀποστήσαντες τὴν φροντίδα, καὶ ἀποφοιτῶντες εἰσάπαν τῶν εἰκαίων περισπασμῶν. «Ἑπτὰ ἑβδομάδας ἐτῶν,» τοῦτ' ἔστιν, αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἐφ' ἑτοίμοις τε καὶ προκειμένοις διατελέσομεν ἀγαθοῖς, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τοῖς παρὰ Θεοῦ καὶ πνευματικοῖς ἐντρυφῶντές τε καὶ ἑορτάζοντες. Καιρὸς γὰρ ἀφέσεως ἔσται πᾶσιν ἡμῖν τοῖς ἀνὰ πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην, ὁ ἐν ἐσχάτοις, ὅτε καὶ ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ δραμεῖται κτῆσιν, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, εἰς τὸν αὐτῷ πρέποντα κλῆρον, καὶ ἐκνεμηθέντα παρὰ Θεοῦ. Διαφορὰ γὰρ ὥσπερ ἐστὶ τῆς τῶν ἁγίων ζωῆς, οὕτω καὶ γερῶν, ἀναλόγως τοῖς ἑκάστου κατορθώμασιν ἐπιμετροῦντος Θεοῦ τὴν ἀντέκτισιν. Διαμέμνηται δὲ καὶ τῆς τὰ τοιάδε διαγγελλούσης σάλπιγγος. Καιρὸς γὰρ ἡμῖν σαββατισμοῦ, ὡς ἐν Χριστῷ δηλονότι, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀφέσεώς τε καὶ κληροδοσίας, ἡ διὰ σάλπιγγός τε καὶ ἀγγέλου φωνῆς ἐσομένη κατὰ καιροὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναβίωσις, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἡ λαμπρὰ τῶν ἁγίων πληθὺς, ἀκούσεται λέγοντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ· «Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ Πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου,» ἧς καὶ ἡμᾶς γένοιτο τυχεῖν χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ Θεοῦ, καὶ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι' οὗ καὶ μεθ' οὗ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ ἡ δόξα σὺν ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
pass_a_gloss: (saying in) Leviticus to the hierophant Moses: 'Speak to the sons of Israel and you will say to them: If you come into the land which I give you, and you give rest to the land which I give you, Sabbaths to the Lord; six years you will sow your field, and six years you will prune your vineyard, and you will gather its fruit, but in the seventh year Sabbaths. A rest will be for your land, Sabbaths to the Lord. Your field you will not sow, and your vineyard you will not prune, and the things coming up of themselves of your field you will not reap, and the grape of your sanctification you will not gather; a year of rest will be for the land, and the Sabbaths of the land will be foods for you, and for your servant, and for your maidservant, and for your hired man, and for the sojourner lying near you; and for your beasts, and for the wild animals in your land, all its produce will be for food. And you will number for yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and there will be for you seven weeks of years, nine and forty years. And you will announce with the voice of a trumpet in all your land, in the seventh month on the tenth of the month. On the day of the propitiation you will announce with a trumpet in all your land. And you will sanctify the year, the fiftieth year, and you will proclaim release on the land to all those dwelling in it. A year of release, this will be a signal for you, and each one will go off into his possession, and each into his family will go off.' Do you understand then how the law permits plowing and sowing and being caretakers of vineyards before the seventh? But to be let go of the care about these it has ordered at the seventh. For we are let go, keeping Sabbath in Christ and having removed the care of earthly things, and departing altogether from the vain distractions. 'Seven weeks of years', that is, ages of the ages, we will continue in goods ready and lying before us, plainly delighting and feasting in the spiritual things from God. For a time of release will be for all of us throughout the whole inhabited world, the one in the last times, when also each will run into his own possession, that is, into the lot befitting him and distributed by God. For as there is a difference of the life of the saints, so also of the prizes, God measuring out the repayment proportionally to the achievements of each. And he makes mention also of the trumpet announcing such things. For a time for us of Sabbath-keeping, namely as in Christ, and also of release and of allotment of inheritance, is the coming back to life from the dead which will be through trumpet and voice of angel in due times, in which also the bright multitude of the saints will hear Christ saying: 'Come, the blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world', which may we too attain by the grace and love of man of the Lord and God and our Savior Jesus Christ, through whom and with whom to God and Father the glory with Holy Spirit now and always and to the ages of the ages. Amen.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …Leviticus to Moses, the revealer of sacred things: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel, and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, and you give the land that I am giving you rest, sabbaths to the Lord: six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its fruit; but in the seventh year, sabbaths. It shall be a rest for your land, sabbaths to the Lord. You shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard, and what springs up of itself in your field you shall not reap, and the grapes of your consecration you shall not gather; it shall be a year of rest for the land. And the sabbaths of the land shall be food for you, and for your servant, and for your maidservant, and for your hired worker, and for the sojourner who stays with you; and for your cattle and for the wild animals in your land all its produce shall be for food. And you shall count for yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and you shall have seven weeks of years, forty-nine years. And you shall proclaim with the sound of the trumpet in all your land, in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month; on the day of atonement you shall proclaim with the trumpet in all your land. And you shall sanctify the year, the fiftieth year, and proclaim release in the land to all who live in it. It shall be a year of release; it shall be a signal for you, and each one shall go back to his possession, and each shall go back to his family’ (Leviticus 25:2–10).

Do you understand, then, how the law allows plowing and sowing and tending vineyards before the seventh year? But it commanded release from care for these things in the seventh. For we are released as we keep sabbath in Christ, having removed our care from earthly things and departed altogether from vain distractions. ‘Seven weeks of years,’ that is, ages of ages, we shall spend among goods that are ready and set before us, delighting, plainly, in the spiritual things that come from God, and keeping festival. For there will be a time of release for all of us throughout the whole inhabited world, the time at the end, when each will also run to his own possession, that is, to the portion that befits him and has been allotted by God. For as there is a difference in the life of the saints, so also in their rewards, since God measures out the repayment in proportion to each one’s good deeds. He also makes mention of the trumpet that proclaims such things. For our time of sabbath-keeping, in Christ, plainly, and of release and of the giving of the inheritance, is the return to life from the dead, which will come in its own time through the trumpet and the voice of an angel (1 Thessalonians 4:16), in which the shining multitude of the saints will hear Christ saying, ‘Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world’ (Matthew 25:34). May we too attain it, by the grace and loving-kindness of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, through whom and with whom be glory to God the Father, with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: ἱεροφάντης, one who shows holy things; avoids the pagan-cult sense of 'hierophant'.
Standard name of the day; book convention.
The Greek ends with Cyril's own prayer and doxology; the old English replaced it with an invented exchange.
